source_text: Sacerdos exorabit eum ante Dominum, et dimittetur ei. Christus pontifex noster. Amen.
thought_title: The priest's prayer and Christ as our high priest
orientation: Origen is explaining the priest's role in atonement, identifying the priest who prays for the sinner with Christ as our high priest.
pass_a_gloss: The priest will pray for him before the Lord, and it will be forgiven to him. Christ is our high priest. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary specifies 'priest' for sacerdos, and the definite article is needed in English to mark the subject of the sentence.
The verb exoro means to pray earnestly or entreat on behalf of someone; the future tense is preserved.

choices.english: it will be forgiven to him
choices.why: The passive of dimitto in a theological context means forgiveness of sin; the dative ei is rendered as 'to him' to preserve the construction.
rejected: it will be released to him

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'high priest' for pontifex, and this is the key Christological identification in the passage.

bible_refs.note: Sacerdos exorabit eum ante Dominum, et dimittetur ei

pass_b_english: The priest will pray for him before the Lord, and it will be forgiven to him (Leviticus 4:26). Christ is our high priest. Amen.
